title: 960 hPa in the Bering Sea
subtitle: The deepest storm on the network this season · 6–16 October 2026
intro: On 8 October a buoy 142 nautical miles north-northeast of Attu recorded the lowest pressure anywhere on the network in six months. Watch the low sweep across the Bering Sea, the wind follow it, and the cold wake it leaves in the ocean behind it.

events.text: 46070's barometer begins a {dhPa:58.4} fall in 24 hours ({hPa:1018.9} → {hPa:960.5})
The low takes hold — 46070 is {dhPa:9.0} below its normal and still falling
46070 bottoms out at {hPa:959.4} — the lowest pressure anywhere on the network this season
On land, the exposed Nikolski White Alice site gusts to {ms:38.1} — hilltop exposure, about twice its neighbour
Cold wake: 46070 has cooled {dC:2.27} since the storm arrived — {dC:1.73} beyond the normal autumn cooling
46070 is back on its seasonal trend, 6 days after its coldest point
The low fades from the network
6 days after the storm passed, 46073 is still {dC:0.99} colder than its seasonal trend
